subject: MSA & Order Form — proposed risk transfer options and OSS/model carveouts
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@lumenai.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: LumenAI Legal <legal@lumenai.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: MSA/Order Form — IP defense & indemnity ask

Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the MSA and order form. We're reviewing your team's redlines and have one major open item on IP/third-party claims we need to resolve before legal signs off on the purchase order. High level: we need the customer to be protected for third-party IP claims arising from the outputs of Redwood models when those outputs are used directly by our regulated customers.

Specifically, LumenAI is asking for:
- A defend-and-indemnify (for third-party IP claims) that covers customer-facing outputs produced by Redwood-served models (including cases where output is later incorporated into LumenAI products).
- Defense control to sit with the customer (or their counsel) in certain high-exposure matters.
- No carveout for generated output unless Redwood can demonstrate indemnity via insurance or unlimited liability, which we understand may not be acceptable.

Given the regulated nature of our customers, limiting the customer's protection is difficult for procurement. Please see attached — we shared a marked-up redline with our proposed language. We also need current SOC2 evidence and a short list of any model components that include third-party proprietary code.

Attachment: LumenAI_proposed_redline.docx

Can we schedule a quick call to walk through the position? Ideally we close language this week so legal can clear procurement.

Best,
Olivia Chen
Head of Legal Ops
LumenAI

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@lumenai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, LumenAI Legal <legal@lumenai.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form — IP defense & indemnity ask

Olivia — thanks, received and appreciate the context. Quick response below and a proposed counter-redline attached.

Summary of Redwood position (high level):
- We understand Lumen's need to manage downstream/regulatory risk. Redwood can offer a narrow indemnity for third-party IP claims but with the following guardrails:
  * Exclusions for (i) Customer modifications or customer-supplied data; (ii) open source components and third-party libraries that Redwood did not author; and (iii) claims arising solely from Customer's incorporation or transformation of model outputs.
  * Liability cap tied to the Order Form (12 months of fees or $1M minimum) — we can discuss increasing this to match the deal economics, but unlimited liability is not something we can accept across the platform.
  * Defense control: we propose a shared control approach — Redwood may select counsel but we agree to reasonable cooperation and an approval window for client counsel in high-stakes matters. This limits duplicative defense spend while preserving customer input on strategy.
- Options to bridge the gap: (a) escrow fund (for larger enterprise buys) to supplement the cap, or (b) a minimum insurance requirement (certificate of insurance naming LumenAI as an additional insured) with commercially reasonable limits.

Attached: redlined_MSA_kp_v2.docx (highlights proposed carveouts and the shared-control language)
Attached: SOC2_2026.pdf (attestation)
Attached: MSA_exhibitA-evidence-list.xlsx (catalog of third-party components and provenance)

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick 30-min sync today or tomorrow to align on whether Lumen can work with carveouts + insurance/escrow option.
2) If Lumen insists on customer control + broad indemnity, we escalate to pricing team for a risk-based uplift (we may need capacity/insurance gating).

If you want, Marissa can run contract language alternatives and Aditya can confirm operational feasibility for escrow/insurance integrations.

Thanks — kimberly

--

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@lumenai.com>

Cc: LumenAI Legal <legal@lumenai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-17T13:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form — IP defense & indemnity ask

Kimberly — thanks for the quick counter and attachments. A few points from our side before a call:

1) Carveouts are helpful but we need explicit language protecting our customers when the only causal chain is Redwood model output. For regulated customers that means they cannot assume responsibility for defects or third-party claims that stem from the output.

2) Shared defense control is unlikely to pass procurement for several of our customers — they will push for customer control or at least the right to appoint lead counsel. If Redwood is insistent on selecting counsel, we need stronger metrics (e.g., counsel rating, conflict rules, expense caps) and an irrevocable approval window for customer-appointed counsel.

3) On cap: 12 months of fees / $1M feels low given potential downstream liabilities. Procurement is asking for either a higher cap tied to ARR or an explicit insurance minimum (we'd expect a $5M policy for this theorem).

4) If Redwood can accept a narrowly scoped indemnity for "Outputs" (defined narrowly), and provide a $5M insurance certificate, we can likely get procurement to accept shared control with additional guardrails.

We uploaded our proposed redline in the attachment and highlighted the "Outputs" language we care about. Can your team push a firm position on the insurance/escrow options? After that we can take the updated redline back to procurement.

Best,
Olivia

- Aditya: confirm operational impact and feasibility for an escrow workflow and what minimum escrow sizing would look like (estimate for deal: 3–6 months of fees as an escrow). Also confirm if we can pass a $5M CI requirement (how many customers trigger additional underwriting / pricing).
